title: Finite free scalar extension and the canonical strict derived limit
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $R_T\to S_T$ a map of sheaves of commutative rings on a small skeleton of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with a finite $R_T$-module basis of $S_T$. Use unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], scalar extension $C=-\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and total derived inverse limit of strict towers, with its projection-normalized Roos realization [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Extension of scalars on strict towers is termwise. For every object $K_\bullet$ in the derived category of strict $R_T$-module towers, the canonical comparison
$$\lambda_{K_\bullet}:C(R\varprojlim K_\bullet)\longrightarrow R\varprojlim(CK_\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S_T)$, natural on the derived category of entire towers. The comparison is the derived version of the canonical scalar/limit map, not an arbitrary map between cones. In a chosen finite basis, after restriction to $R_T$, it is the finite-sum/product reindexing on both product coordinates of the Roos complex; it intertwines $1-s$, where $s((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$. It is $S_T$-linear and independent of the basis. For another finite free ring-sheaf extension $S_T\to U_T$, the two composites obtained by these comparisons agree with $\lambda$ for $R_T\to U_T$ under the balanced derived tensor associator; the identity extension gives the identity. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness or normalization of $K_\bullet$ is assumed.

source.place: (1), derived inverse limits and finite sums; returned step 2 limit argument

proof.text: Use the finite-basis presentation of ordinary scalar extension after restriction. Restriction reflects isomorphisms and preserves limits, and the finite power functor preserves limits. Thus finite-free scalar extension preserves finite limits and countable products; its tensor adjunction gives finite colimits. The corresponding assertions for towers follow pointwise.

Exact countable products on the specified small pro-etale model allow strictRoosDerivation to construct a single derived-limit functor L_R and normalized rho_R for each R, with the required universal right-derived property.

Use the canonical additive Roos comparison. Preservation of countable products makes it an iso. Its product projections, transition compatibility and both cone-coordinate formulas are the standard additive Roos formulas. Fully faithful whiskering with localization descends the rho-conjugate cone iso to the derived comparison. The zero-first-coordinate inclusion and product projections prove its ordinary-limit normalization. Naturality of the finite-basis iso proves the requested coordinate formula.

The ordinary balanced associator and unitor have the prescribed pure-tensor normalization. Horizontal coherence and the identity formula for the actual additive Roos comparison give equal cone maps. At objects in the image of Q, expand the derived associator or unitor using exact-functor factorization. Apply naturality, cancel adjacent rho and factorization inverse pairs, and use the cone equation. Full faithfulness of localization whiskering extends these equalities to every entire derived tower.
